problem: Value-map ZSON controllers (VLFM, ASCENT) are purely reactive: they have no recourse at structural impasses (stalls, far frontiers, exhausted frontiers, wrong floor) and fuse detections without verification. LLM/VLM-guided systems call the model on a fixed schedule from current evidence only, cannot re-examine earlier views, and leave call governance and failure fallback unspecified.
motivation: Most structural impasses depend on earlier observations the reactive controller no longer keeps. Making the robot's own past views the object of deliberation, with bounded and fail-open invocation, could improve success without simply spending more model calls.
key_idea: Keep a reactive value-map controller running every step that writes a coordinate-anchored memory (semantic grid plus pose-tagged keyframes), and wake an event-triggered, budget-bounded ReAct agent at structural impasses to reason over text first and recall views only when needed, with all failures returning to the reactive layer.
insight: Gain comes from when deliberation fires and what it reads, not from more model access. Always-Deliberate makes the most calls yet scores below Greedy Frontier. One-Shot (all images in one query) and w/o Semantic Grid (same call budget) both fall back to roughly the Greedy Frontier SR, so adaptive evidence acquisition and the abstract memory tier are both necessary. The failure-class decomposition shows deliberation spreads gains across FP, no-frontier and FN, while the semantic grid mainly prevents premature no-frontier stops.
method: Reactive controller: ASCENT/VLFM-style occupancy, value (BLIP-2 similarity), semantic and object maps, detection ensemble, DD-PPO point-goal execution, stair FSM; runs every step.
Per-detection verification gate: a VLM sees the cropped candidate frame and accepts/rejects each goal detection before fusion into the object map, so false positives cannot be fused permanently.
Semantic grid: 8x8-pixel (0.4 m) cells storing room-type vote histograms, keyframe index rings and object instances; an instance is confirmed and retrievable after ≥2 sightings.
Keyframe store: bounded per-floor low-res thumbnails with pose, floor, step, room and objects; retrieval ranks by cos(Δβ)−λd within FOV with a fallback ladder ending in text-only.

Event-triggered ReAct loops: contact stalls (call-free replan tier, then VLM escape heading), distant frontiers (text-first round, then ≤2 recalled images), frontier exhaustion (rescan montage of ≤8 keyframes for overlooked passages), floor change (text summary).

Budgets and arbitration: ≤3 rounds and ≤2 images per invocation, ≤20 calls and ≤10 image calls per run, 180 s watchdog, circuit breaker; persistent deliberative targets; priority arbiter; every failure returns to the reactive base.

setting.backbone: ASCENT-style reactive controller (BLIP-2, D-FINE/GroundingDINO/RAM detectors, MobileSAM, Places365, RedNet, DD-PPO) plus an external VLM service (unspecified) for deliberation and verification
setting.action_space: discrete actions via point-goal policy toward frontier/goal targets, plus short macro-actions for recovery
setting.simulator: Habitat (Habitat-Sim/Lab 0.3.1) on HM3D v1 and MP3D

numbers_note: The LaTeX text uses macros (e.g. \OursHMSR, \OursMPSR) for all numeric values and the tables contain no literal numbers, so exact SR/SPL values are not available in the provided text.
results: The full system reaches the highest SR among compared zero-shot methods (ZSON, ESC, L3MVN, VLFM, SG-Nav, ASCENT) on HM3D v1 val and MP3D val, and also leads on SPL. Ablations show Greedy Frontier loses SR points in a paired comparison, and Always-Deliberate, One-Shot and w/o Semantic Grid all lose SR against the full system.
limitations: Depends on an external VLM API, with latency and per-run call caps; a 180 s watchdog is needed for slow decisions.
Evaluated only in Habitat simulation (HM3D, MP3D), with no real-robot experiments.
Ablations are on HM3D only; the paper reports no per-category analysis or sensitivity to the trigger thresholds.
